name: Hotel Maria Cristina
positioning: Hotel Maria Cristina, a Luxury Collection Hotel: a Belle Epoque hotel opened in 1912 beside the river Urumea in San Sebastian, with river and sea views
best_for: Travelers who want a historic Belle Epoque hotel with river and sea views
Art and film lovers drawn to the Eduardo Chillida and Bette Davis suites
Families or groups needing family rooms or connecting multi-bedroom suites

facts.text: The hotel is named for Spain's regent queen, mother of King Alfonso XIII.
The hotel is built in the Belle Epoque style, like the city hall and Victoria Eugenia Theater near La Concha beach.
The hotel has a river setting and sea views.
The interior is furnished with a soft color scheme in gray, mauve and turquoise.
The suites are decorated with marble fireplaces, glass lamps and velvet turquoise armchairs.
The Bette Davis Suite is dedicated to the actress and is adorned with her photos.
Some suites have views of the river or old town, and some rooms have terraces.
Family accommodation can host up to four guests.
Multi Bedroom Suites with connecting setups are available for larger groups or families.
Dry Martini by Javier de las Muelas serves afternoon tea, classic and signature cocktails, and traditional Basque pintxos.
Amelia by chef Paulo Airaudo offers contemporary fine dining inspired by the Basque Sea.

highlights.text: The hotel was designed by architect Charles Mewes, who was responsible for the Ritz in Madrid and Paris.
The hotel sits beside the river Urumea, with views of Rafael Moneo's Kursaal building and the Cantabrian Sea beyond.
Guests in the Eduardo Chillida Suite receive tickets to the Chillida Leku museum.
The rooftop Royal Terrace Suite has expansive terraces with river views.
The concierge wears the Les Clefs d'Or insignia of the international concierge society.

considerations.text: Rooms do not have a coffee or tea maker.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have smaller room sizes.
